text: The second half of RR:215 blocker ① — '20+ samples show no XP formula either' — is FALSE. The complete XP award function is in the web payload at §1t68s0§.as:185-209, and it is called on kill at :888 as §1t12070s0§(StatsManager.getLevel(), this.level, this.xp, false). The rule, read straight off the lines: award 0 if the enemy level is at or below a level-scaled floor (§1t12068s0§, :113-128: 0 below player level 6, then lvl - floor(lvl/10) - 5 under 40, lvl - floor(lvl/5) - 1 under 60, else lvl - 9); award 0 if the enemy is more than 3 levels above you (:191-193); otherwise base = enemy xp, scaled UP by (1 + 0.05 * levelGap) when the enemy out-levels you (:198) and DOWN by (1 - underGap / §1t12069s0§()) when you out-level it (:202, divisor 5 below player level 8, 6 below 10, 7 below 12, 8 below 16, ...), then doubled if the boolean flag is set (:204-206). The enemy's own xp is not a table lookup at all — it is closed-form: §1t68s0§.as:237 'this.xp = this.level * 2 + 20;' (same at :271). Nothing here needs measuring. This is why npcdata.xml carries ZERO <xp> tags (grep -c '<xp>' = 0) — there was never a per-NPC xp row to find, which is exactly the shape of evidence that made 20+ video samples look like 'no formula'.

text: Correction to nf4, and it makes the XP model STRONGER than nf4 claims. Per-kill base XP is not read from a data file at all: §1t68s0§.as:237 sets 'this.xp = this.level * 2 + 20;' inside init(), and :271 repeats 'this.xp = param1 * 2 + 20;' inside setLevel(), and that same this.xp is what :888 hands to the XP function. Confirming from the data side: reference/extracted/npcdata.xml contains ZERO '<xp>' elements (grep -c '<xp>' returns 0; the file's tag census runs <id> 1273, <lvl> 1049, <skill> 647, <npc> 495, <attack> 406, <hp> 403, <defense> 394 — no xp tag anywhere). So the whole per-kill XP model is a closed-form function of two integers, mob level and player level, with no data dependency: xp = 0 if mobLevel <= greyLevel(playerLevel) or mobLevel - playerLevel > 3; else (2*mobLevel + 20) scaled by (1 + 0.05*(mobLevel-playerLevel)) or (1 - (playerLevel-mobLevel)/zeroDifference(playerLevel)), doubled for elites. Both helper curves are also in code: §1t68s0§.as:113-129 greyLevel is a piecewise ladder ('lvl - floor(lvl/10) - 5' below 40, 'lvl - floor(lvl/5) - 1' below 60, 'lvl - 9' above) and :131+ zeroDifference is a level-banded step table.

So 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' is the unavailable-state readout of a gate, not the absence of a mechanic. Independent corroboration that switching in battle exists at all: shs3_android/scripts/GameEngine.as:584 is an in-game tip that says so in plain English. Note also that the string 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' occurs in ZERO extracted artifacts — absent from reference/extracted/ui_strings.txt and from the 2,533-entry strings.json — it survives only in video-study prose, so no artifact currently pins its exact trigger. THE FRAME IS NOT BEING OVERRIDDEN HERE: the label is real and stays; what falls is the inference drawn from it.
